patch.value: Custom statuses registered without a lifecycle role are silently orphaned from every work-selection surface

pm schema add-status accepts a status with no --role and registers it with an empty roles list, with no warning. Items in that status then exist but are invisible to the entire agent work-selection surface, and no diagnostic reports the condition. Reproduced on a clean sandbox workspace against dist build 2026.7.25.

Repro: pm schema add-status needs_review (exit 0, no warning; schema/statuses.json records {"id":"needs_review"} with no roles key, unlike every built-in which carries roles such as active/terminal/default_open). pm create --status needs_review succeeds. Then: pm next -> recommended null, ready 0, candidates 0, blocked 0. pm context -> active_items 0, open 0. pm list-open -> 0 rows. pm validate -> ok true with no role-related warning. pm health -> ok true, all 10 checks ok. The item IS visible to pm stats by_status and to pm list --status needs_review, so it is not terminal either: it is lifecycle-orphaned.

Control: registering the same status with --role active makes the identical item recommended by pm next (ready 1, candidates 1) and active in pm context (active_items 1). The single missing role flag is the whole difference between fully tracked work and work no agent will ever be offered.

Second half of the same class: pm context summary.open and summary.in_progress are computed by matching the literal built-in status ids open and in_progress (src/cli/commands/context.ts around lines 2645-2654 call normalizeStatusInput with hardcoded "open"/"in_progress"), while summary.active_items is role-derived. In the --role active control above the result is active_items 1 with open 0 and in_progress 0, so the summary arithmetic silently stops adding up in any workspace that uses a custom active status. Agents read that summary to decide whether work exists.

This directly contradicts epic pm-8jdc acceptance ('any project archetype can model its domain end-to-end with custom statuses without code changes') and is exactly the class the pm-pww8ax dogfood ratchet exists to catch: custom statuses are at zero adoption in this workspace, so the orphaning has never been exercised.

pm schema add-status either requires a lifecycle role or defaults to a documented role and reports which role was applied; registering a role-less status is impossible or warns loudly at registration time. pm validate and pm health each gain a check that reports every registered status carrying no lifecycle role, with the affected item ids. pm context summary.open and summary.in_progress are derived from lifecycle roles rather than the literal built-in status ids, so active_items reconciles with its component buckets in a workspace using custom active statuses. A regression test registers a custom status per lifecycle role and asserts next/context/list-open/list-blocked classify its items consistently with the equivalent built-in status.
